newsitem.title: INDIA: India TMC chief to decide course within two days.
newsitem.headline: India TMC chief to decide course within two days.

text.p: The president of former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) will decide within two days whether to join Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition government, a party leader said.

"We expect Mr.Moopanar to take a decision in a day or two," TMC's general secretary, Jayanthi Natarajan, told reporters in the southern city of Madras, where the party's executive committee held a meeting.
"The issue is quite complex and the feelings were running quite high during the meeting. It is not a simple decision to take," Natarajan said.
Earlier, the TMC's executive had authorised the party chief, G.K. Moopanar, to take a final decision on joining a new United Front government formed last week.
The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and next prime minister.
But it continued to offer support to the new government.
Party officials said TMC legislators in the Tamil Nadu assembly as well as district presidents pressed Moopanar at Sunday's meeting to keep the regional party out of Gujral's government.
They argued that joining Gujral's government would limit TMC's options in competing with the state's ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), also a part of the alliance.
"Eighty percent were against joining the government. Their arguments were based on Tamil Nadu politics.," a TMC leader said.

Gujral was elected to win back support from the Congress party, which offered vital backing to the United Front to keep out a common rival, the rightwing Hindu nationalist, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The Congress wanted the alliance to replace ousted Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whom it helped topple in a parliamentary confidence vote on April 11.
